gen-silkscreen-gf-fauna-one: Fauna One reads dignified and literary, its tall middle band tucked between shallow ascenders and descenders. Silkscreen sits above it as lo-fi pixel spaghetti, so the page moves from retro game screen to quiet bookshelf.
gen-silkscreen-gf-glegoo:
Glegoo reads refined, with big counters and curves that stay wide open.

Silkscreen is best at playful, spaced-out retro punch, while Glegoo is best at carrying a steady, tall-lowercase text serif line without fuss.
gen-silkscreen-gf-hanuman: Pixel-bright and a bit nostalgic, Silkscreen spaces every letter out like a lo-fi arcade sign. And Hanuman follows in a refined, high-waisted serif, its s terminals set wide, giving the page a traditional anchor.
gen-silkscreen-gf-kadwa: Classic and editorial, Kadwa has open-ended curves and a larger-than-usual x-height under Silkscreen's retro pixel heading. Shrink the heading and its spaghetti lines get fussy.
gen-silkscreen-gf-noticia-text: Noticia Text reads literary and dignified, with a big visible entrance into every curve and lowercase filling most of the height. Noticia Text against Silkscreen's wirelike, single-thickness strokes is the pair's strongest quality: retro lightness over a classic serif that stays grounded.
gen-silkscreen-gf-piazzolla: Silkscreen does lo-fi, retro attitude best, with room around every letter you can almost feel. But Piazzolla is the one for authority, its lowercase nearly matching the capitals in a refined classic serif.
gen-silkscreen-gf-pridi: Refined, first of all, thanks to Pridi's proud, almost capital-sized small letters. Silkscreen's lo-fi spaghetti lines against that text serif make the strongest quality here: playful retro on top, polished calm beneath.
gen-silkscreen-gf-scope-one:
Scope One brings stubby ascenders beside a big x-height.

Silkscreen's retro, lo-fi spacing sits on top, and the text serif's counters spill into surrounding space, so nudging the body size up lets that openness really show.
gen-silkscreen-gf-slabo-13px: Slabo 13px has large open counters in its tall a, e and s, and a bookish, dignified feel. Yet Silkscreen does the lo-fi retro spacing best, while the classic serif body handles clear, rounded reading.
gen-silkscreen-gf-suwannaphum: Silkscreen draws wirelike retro lines where stems match the hairlines because there are none, giving a lo-fi, spaced-out look. Suwannaphum, a dignified serif with a high x-height, makes a longer read feel steady.
